Comparisons 2, 3 and 4 stayed unknown because they carry no applicability condition, so the other case's probe event is scored as a failed admission instead of being outside applicability (diagnostics: 'No corresponding prerequisite events reached: trimmed_setup/ca_setup' at the control probe, and the mirror for untrimmed_setup at the trimmed probe). interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds; it then fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot over and over. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps the suffix above the snapshot index (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader can only walk nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372). Retained observations, two independent runs of the same two-case experiment (executions 5e63769a85ac4b5f90ebe12a4ddcc5fd and d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, both exit 0 with both cases passing): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) records the victim's cached claim at (95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnect the probe event (index 14) records the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (repeated_snapshot_installs true, comparison 0 complete and holds), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 through newly committed and applied writes (victim_not_caught_up true, comparison 1 complete and holds on the same probe), the cached claim still (95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and one stable leader set for the whole window with the victim's term fixed at 3. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which attributes the stall to the install path together with the trimmed leader log rather than to the mere existence of a stale suffix. The residual uncertainty is narrow and mechanical: comparisons 2, 3 and 4 are not yet decided because those definitions lack an applicability condition, so the other case's probe is treated as a missing admission; the third experiment adds the tag-scoped condition and is the discriminator for a complete verdict. Limits: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 versus a large control, a 3s window with one write per 250ms sample, and a single induced partition; the follower's commit index was never advanced by the install path (0 while applied was 83) and is treated as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect; the vote-side consequence of the stale claim is source-derived and unmeasured because no election occurred; the starved state would end if the leader later shipped a snapshot whose index exceeded the follower's cached claim, and no such snapshot was taken in either run because automatic snapshotting was disabled; the monotonic-store variant deletes the suffix instead of keeping it and needs its own receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.
Probe fields are read from the follower's cached state and its log store on the same process; the receipt is needed before treating the numbers as retained observations.

Basis, source side: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail), getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry), the non-monotonic compaction path cannot remove a suffix that still lies above the snapshot index (src_compaction), every prev-log check then misses or mismatches so the leader only decrements nextIndex one step at a time (src_replicate_failure) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound and the leader re-sends the newest snapshot, after which nextIndex is reset to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result). Basis, retained receipt (execution d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, exit 0, both generated cases passed): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) recorded the victim's cached last log claim (index 95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at index 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnecting, the probe event (index 14) recorded the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (leader_snapshot_is_unchanged true), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 with new entries committed and applied elsewhere, the cached claim still (index 95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and exactly one stable leader set over the window. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (index 95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which excludes the mere existence of the stale suffix as the cause. The raw retained values therefore support the account, but the comparison-level verdict, and with it the formal conclusion, is still pending. interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.
Probe fields are read from the follower's cached state and its log store on the same process; the receipt is needed before treating the numbers as retained observations.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index is not above its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds and cannot accept any further log entry from that leader, so the cluster keeps re-shipping the same snapshot while the follower's applied state stays at the snapshot index. Basis, source side: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail), getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry), the non-monotonic compaction path cannot remove a suffix that still lies above the snapshot index (src_compaction), every prev-log check then misses or mismatches so the leader only decrements nextIndex one step at a time (src_replicate_failure) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound and the leader re-sends the newest snapshot, after which nextIndex is reset to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result). Basis, retained receipt (execution d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, exit 0, both generated cases passed): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) recorded the victim's cached last log claim (index 95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at index 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnecting, the probe event (index 14) recorded the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (leader_snapshot_is_unchanged true), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 with new entries committed and applied elsewhere, the cached claim still (index 95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and exactly one stable leader set over the window. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (index 95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which excludes the mere existence of the stale suffix as the cause. The five declared comparisons resolved unknown, not holds: the admission event ca_setup carried no tag field, so the trimmed_setup/untrimmed_setup alias conditions could not be evaluated and the admission could not be associated ('Missing operation admission fields or identity', 'Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing trimmed_setup.tag'); the successor experiment fixes exactly that field. The raw retained values therefore support the account, but the comparison-level verdict, and with it the formal conclusion, is still pending. Limits: three voters, in-memory log store with a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, a restarted ex-leader whose orphan suffix came from applies it accepted while partitioned, a 3s idle-plus-steady-writes window, and a single induced full partition; the vote-side consequence of the stale claim (knowledge-1) never triggered because no election occurred, the monotonic-store variant deletes the suffix instead of keeping it and needs its own receipt, and nothing here measures whether the state persists beyond the window or whether a larger cluster with several trimmed voters could still repair the node.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier, so a stale log suffix by itself does not stall replication; the trimmed leader log plus the install path is the trigger.

The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: the receipt shows one stable leader set over the whole window and the victim's term fixed at 3, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing in this configuration.
The five declared comparisons are recorded as unknown because the admission event omitted the mode field the alias conditions test; no completed comparison verdict exists yet for this question.
limitations: Measured configuration only: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 versus a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, and a 3s observation window.

The follower's own commit index was never advanced by the install path (recorded as 0 while its applied index was 83); the account treats this as an advertised-state inconsistency and does not treat it as an independent defect.
The vote-side consequence of the stale claim is source-derived (knowledge-1) and unmeasured: no election was induced while the victim held the claim.
The monotonic-store variant, other TrailingLogs values, larger clusters and longer windows are unmeasured; the receipt only shows no repair within the measured window.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds; it then fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot over and over. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps the suffix above the snapshot index (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader can only walk nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372). Retained observations, two independent runs of the same two-case experiment (executions 5e63769a85ac4b5f90ebe12a4ddcc5fd and d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, both exit 0 with both cases passing): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) records the victim's cached claim at (95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnect the probe event (index 14) records the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (repeated_snapshot_installs true, comparison 0 complete and holds), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 through newly committed and applied writes (victim_not_caught_up true, comparison 1 complete and holds on the same probe), the cached claim still (95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and one stable leader set for the whole window with the victim's term fixed at 3. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which attributes the stall to the install path together with the trimmed leader log rather than to the mere existence of a stale suffix.
